newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sanwa Bank sees Y850 bln problem loans. [CORRECTED 08:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sanwa Bank sees Y850 bln problem loans. [CORRECTED 08:10 GMT]

text.p: Japan's Sanwa Bank Ltd said on Friday that it expects to have 850 billion yen in problem loans at the end of March.
(Corrects to show the figure refers to the total of loans and not loan write-offs).
The major city bank said in a statement that it also expects its restructured loans to total 380 billion yen at the end of the month.
Sanwa said it would set aside special reserves for loan write-offs of 410 billion yen for the current business year ending on March 31.

Sanwa said it plans to provide additional financial assistance to its affiliate consumer credit company Aplus Co Ltd in 1996/97, which it said will reduce the bank's total outstanding restructured loans by 200 billion yen.
Earlier, Aplus announced that it expects to receive extra support of about 40 billion yen from Sanwa Bank.
